title: The verb 'to be': jam
subtitle: Present tense conjugation
explanation: In Albanian, the verb 'to be' (jam) is irregular. It must agree with the subject in person and number. The six present tense forms are essential to learn first.
examples: Unë jam student. — I am a student.
Ti je shqiptar. — You are Albanian.
Ai është mësues. — He is a teacher.
Ne jemi miq. — We are friends.
Ata janë këtu. — They are here.

title: The verb 'to have': kam
subtitle: Present tense conjugation
explanation: The verb 'to have' (kam) is also irregular. It is used both for possession and, importantly, as an auxiliary to form perfect tenses later.
examples: Unë kam një libër. — I have a book.
Ti ke kohë? — Do you have time?
Ai ka një makinë. — He has a car.
Ne kemi shumë miq. — We have many friends.

title: Noun Definiteness
subtitle: Indefinite vs. definite articles
explanation: Unlike English, Albanian places its definite article as a suffix (postposed article) at the end of the noun, not before it. Indefinite nouns take no article. This is one of the most distinctive features of Albanian grammar.
examples: Kam një libër. — I have a book. (indefinite)
Libri është interesant. — The book is interesting. (definite)
Shoh një vajzë. — I see a girl. (indefinite)
Vajza është këtu. — The girl is here. (definite)
